archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing and accuracy)
archetype.definition: Burrow wins from the pocket with anticipation and ball placement, getting the ball out quickly and attacking the 10-to-19 yard window rather than creating with his legs.

report.headline: Burrow's intermediate accuracy is carrying the league's most pass-happy offense.
report.take:
This is the Burrow of his best seasons, and the career line backs it up. He led the position in CPOE in 2021 and ranked third in 2024. Now he sits second at 8.45, with a 73% completion rate that is 9.4 points over the qualifier average. Cincinnati leans on him harder than any offense leans on its passer. The team's pass rate over expected is +8, first in the league, and its run game ranks 22nd in EPA. The defense gives up explosive runs and gets dragged into shootouts like the 43-36 win over Tennessee. Volume isn't in question: 302.1 yards a game ranks first, and his 20 touchdowns lead the position.

The engine is the middle of the field. On throws of 10 to 19 air yards he is at 1.005 EPA per attempt with a 21-point CPOE. Throws of 10+ air yards have produced 89.8 EPA, and everything under 10 nets slightly negative. That gap is mostly the screen and swing game. His 42 throws behind the line cost 14.7 EPA, and Chase Brown's 42 targets come in at -0.32 EPA each. Tee Higgins (0.836 per target) and Mike Gesicki (0.791) are where the offense actually lives, with Ja'Marr Chase close behind.

The numbers hide two things. First, the touchdown rate is running hot: 7.5% on the season and 11.8% over the last three games, with 14 red-zone touchdowns on 39 attempts. His 49-TD pace will cool even if the play doesn't. Second, the turnovers are just who he is. Six picks rank 38th of 47, but his interception rate matches the league average. In 2021 and 2022 his interception counts ranked near the bottom too, in seasons that ended among the league's best. The bad-throw rate doubling from last year looks alarming, but 2025's 5% was the outlier. His 10.1% this season is in line with his history and still ranks fourth of 38.

The real growth may be in how he handles pressure. His pressure-to-sack rate has always sat around 29-37%; this year it is 19.6%, seventh-best, behind a line whose QB-hit rate ranks 26th. That is a small sample, but it has kept drives alive. Since a sluggish opening two weeks he has been better every week. The trajectory is a top-five passer with a touchdown rate that will drift back toward his 2024 level.

strengths.title: Owning the 10-to-19 yard window
strengths.body: His intermediate throws are producing over a point of EPA per attempt with a 21-point CPOE. It's the timing-and-placement profile that made him the league's CPOE leader in 2021. The exact rate is unsustainable on 62 attempts, but the skill has held across seasons. With Higgins and Chase both winning, it should stay the offense's best play type.

strengths.title: Accuracy that holds league-wide
strengths.body: A 73% completion rate at 7.85 intended air yards ranks among the top few in CPOE. This isn't a dink-and-dunk inflation. He's completing throws downfield at rates the throw difficulty says he shouldn't. His career CPOE ranks (1st, 3rd) say this is his baseline, not a heater.

strengths.title: Pressure without the sacks
strengths.body: He is pressured on a fairly normal share of dropbacks, behind a line that lets him get hit often. Yet only 19.6% of pressures become sacks, far below his career norm of roughly 30%. The quick 2.66-second release helps, but some of this is sample. Expect it to drift up somewhat, though not back to his worst years.

concerns.title: Dead weight behind the line
concerns.body: The screen and swing game is bleeding value. Throws behind the line of scrimmage have cost 14.7 EPA, and the lead back's targets are deeply negative. This is a scheme and personnel problem more than a Burrow problem. It caps his efficiency when the offense leans on it to protect a lead, which shows in a slightly negative EPA when Cincinnati is up 9+.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate due to cool
concerns.body: Thirteen touchdowns in three games and 14 red-zone scores come on a small sample. Those rates won't hold, even for a passer who threw 43 in 2024. The yardage and efficiency are real; the touchdown spikes are partly variance.

concerns.title: Interceptions are part of the package
concerns.body: Six picks, including three in the Tennessee shootout, rank near the bottom of the position. His rate is league-average, though, and he has posted bottom-tier interception counts in his best seasons. It's the price of attacking tight intermediate windows, not a decline.

trend.note: He opened with negative passing EPA against Tampa Bay and Houston, including five sacks in Houston. Every game since has been clearly positive, and the last three are his best stretch of the year.

nextGame.headline: Sound Falcons defense, but missing pieces where Burrow does damage.
nextGame.body:
Atlanta is a legitimately good pass defense on paper, eighth in overall EPA and fifth against deep throws. It limits opposing WR1s, so this isn't a soft spot for the long ball. The opening is underneath and in the middle. The Falcons have been leaky against WR2s, and Higgins and Chase draw near-identical target volume, so one of them should see the softer side of the coverage. Atlanta's offense is run-heavy and inefficient through the air, which could shorten the game. The 52.5 total and Cincinnati -3 suggest the Book still expects points.

Availability tilts toward Burrow. Linebacker Divine Deablo, an 83%-snap starter, is out, which thins the second level exactly where Burrow's intermediate throws land. Rotational edge Samson Ebukam and part-time corner Billy Bowman Jr. are also out. That chips at a defense that hits quarterbacks often but doesn't finish sacks. On his side, Erick All Jr.'s season-ending ACL removes a part-time tight end without touching Gesicki's role. Andrei Iosivas is tracking toward a return from IR, which would push Dohnte Meyers down the pecking order. Burrow's own week-2 questionable tag is stale; he is listed active and QB1.

keyMatchups.title: Intermediate game versus thinned linebackers
keyMatchups.body: Burrow's best throws come in the 10-to-19 range. Atlanta loses its every-down linebacker, and the throws Deablo would have helped take away are the ones Cincinnati lives on. If the Falcons replace him with a lesser cover player, Higgins and Gesicki over the middle become the pressure point.

keyMatchups.title: The WR2 soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows the second receiver over half a point of EPA per target, one of the worst marks in the league. With Higgins and Chase splitting the top role, whichever draws that coverage should be efficient. The deep shots may be harder to come by against a defense that ranks fifth against them.

keyMatchups.title: Hits without sacks
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta gets home for hits at a top-10 rate but sacks at a middling one, with Ebukam out. That fits Burrow's quick release and his low pressure-to-sack rate this year. Expect him to take some shots but keep drives alive.

nextGame.watch: Whether Cincinnati keeps attacking the middle of the field with Deablo out, or drifts back into the screen game that has cost it all season.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is locked in: the league's heaviest pass lean, a below-average run game and a defense that allows explosive runs all keep him throwing. The accuracy has years of career support, so a top-five efficiency profile is the reasonable expectation. What regresses is the touchdown rate and, probably, the very low pressure-to-sack rate. Expect something like 270 to 315 yards and 2.0 to 2.8 touchdowns a game rather than the four-plus of the last three weeks. Interceptions should settle in the 0.6 to 1.0 range. That's a passer closer to his 2024 shape than his current 49-touchdown pace.

The swing is the offense's short game. If the behind-the-line throws to Brown become more efficient, or simply rarer, his per-play numbers have room to hold up even as the touchdowns cool. An Iosivas return would also give him a usable third receiver.
swingFactors: Touchdown rate normalizing from its hot stretch
How often the screen game to Chase Brown replaces intermediate throws
Protection holding up as pressure-to-sack luck evens out

confidence.note: Seven games, with the depth splits resting on small attempt counts, but his accuracy and volume are backed by his career and his role.
